messages:
Mia (infra): Heads-up — planning a short rolling maintenance in us-east1 GPU pool-3. Target window Wed 02:00-04:00 UTC. Kernel + BMC soft-restarts, 5 nodes drained at a time, prefix/KV cache warmup afterwards. Need to call out dedicated tenants and any known high-concurrency customers. Thoughts?
Sanjay: SGTM. Can we shift to 03:00-05:00 UTC? US traffic dips later, reduces tail risk. Also: exclude dedicated-alpha pool from drains.
Ellie: +1 on excluding alpha. We should run a canary perf pass on one rack 30m prior to the main window to validate NVLink/KV behavior. I'll queue a perf job. @Mia pls add canary + rollback steps to runbook.
Mia (infra): Good call — updated plan: canary 02:45-03:15 UTC, then staggered drains starting 03:20. Dedicated-alpha excluded, priority-tenants pinned. Posting comms after we decide final times.
Tony: Cost heads-up: if we backfill with spot capacity and rewarm caches, egress + model load could spike. Rough estimate +$120/hr if 20 nodes warm from cold. Recommend seeding KV snapshots where possible.
Irene: We have one tenant (acme-inc) that routinely peaks late-night. Their concurrency threshold = 60. Recommend temporarily throttling to 40 for the maintenance window and notify them.
ops-bot: Runbook updated: https://redwood.docs/runbooks/maintenance/gpu-rolling-9149994321 (edited) :white_check_mark:
Sanjay: What is headroom if alpha is excluded? Current pool avg util ~68%. With alpha out we lose ~8% capacity; headroom drops to ~12%. If we exceed 80% we should pre-allocate reserved instances.
Mia (infra): Plan: reserve 10 standby instances in us-east1 for live backfill. If utilization >80% we trigger cross-region routing to eu-west3 and enable model-variant fallback (gptq -> int8) for non-critical routes.
Ellie: Can someone update Console SLO heatmap and set alert threshold at 75% for the window? I want early signal on scheduling pressure, not just 90%.
Tony: I'll add a finance note and create ticket FIN-4821 with cost forecast and mitigation options.
Sanjay: Oncall: @Irene are you able to cover 02:30-04:30 for escalation/rollback?
Irene: Yep, I'm oncall. I'll watch tail-latency, error-rate, and token throughput. If p50/p95 tail latency stays >150ms for more than 10m we rollback to previous kernel and rehydrate from snapshots.
Mia (infra): Thanks. I'll publish tenant comms 6h before window with explicit throttle instructions and contact points. Also adding a quickplaybook: `if pool_util>85% -> trigger reserved -> notify #support-prod`.
deploy-bot: Scheduled task created: maintenance-9149994321, canary job queued.
Sanjay: FYI — I pushed a small script to ops-tools to pre-seed KV snapshots: `scripts/kv_seed.sh --pool pool-3 --snap latest` (run 30m before canary).
Ellie: I'll run the NVLink perf job and post results in thread. If the canary shows any degraded interconnect bandwidth we abort and reschedule.
Mia (infra): Perfect. Last note: we'll enable quiet-mode routing for best-effort routes so we avoid noisy neighbor retries. Posting final confirmed times in #status 6h before. :rocket:
